fixed.title: The seg_contig cursor is advanced on a private copy and thrown away, so every epoch re-reads the identical head of every area and the exposure guard reports a number the run did not experience.
fixed.what_changed: DEFECT: the seg_contig cursor was never persisted (critical). Line ~973 `cursors = dict(areas.cursors)` copied the dict; the copy was advanced and thrown away, so areas.cursors stayed all-zero forever and every epoch re-read the same head of every area. FIX: bind the SAME dict object (`cursors = areas.cursors`, no copy) -- Areas is a frozen dataclass but `cursors` is an ordinary mutable dict VALUE, so mutating it in place is not a frozen-field reassignment and every write now lands on the one dict the composition root holds across every epoch's draw_stream call. Also changed the write-back from the unbounded `start + want` to `(start + want) % len(body)` so the value a checkpoint would carry is bounded.
fixed.proof: Ran /tmp/.../scratchpad (verify cursor persistence): DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000 DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 DATA_RESAMPLE=1 DATA_STREAM_BYTES=40000, epochs 0/1/2 through the real open_areas->data_plan->draw_stream path on one shared `areas` object (as the composition root does). BEFORE (git HEAD): areas.cursors stayed {'eng': 0} after every call and epoch0.bytes == epoch1.bytes (byte-identical). AFTER: areas.cursors printed {'eng': 40000} after epoch 0 and {'eng': 80000} after epoch 1; epoch0.bytes == body[0:40000] -> True; epoch1.bytes == body[40000:80000] -> True; epoch2.bytes == body[80000:120000] -> True; epoch0.bytes == epoch1.bytes -> False. The cursor now genuinely advances and each epoch reads a distinct, contiguous slice of the body, matching the docstring's 'PERSISTS ACROSS EPOCHS' claim.

fixed.title: DATA_DRAW=planned (the new shipped default) measurably worsens the pre-existing estimate-vs-realized gap in Gate data.splice_window, which H58's own rationale for defaulting to planned never accounts for
fixed.what_changed: data_plan runs before a single byte is drawn, so data.splice_window's mean_seg cannot become 'measured, not estimated' without moving the check to after the draw (turning a startup gate into a report line). Instead gave the Gate a `reason` caveat -- always present, not just under DATA_DRAW=uniform -- stating plainly that this is a startup PREDICTION, that under the shipped 'planned' law draw_stream additionally truncates to each area's remaining per-phase budget (not just the phase bound), and quoting the measured 8-seed false-negative rate (8/8 under planned vs 6/8 under uniform at the same sweep) and the phase-count-scaling gap (7.6/10.4/17.7/32.3% under planned vs 3.7/4.9/10.0/17.9% under uniform at 8/10/20/40 phases), mirroring the caveat pattern exposure_max/exposure_skew already carry for the same law.
fixed.proof: Read the new `reason=splice_caveat` text on the returned Gate('data.splice_window', ...) object in a live data_plan() call -- confirmed present on every arm (not conditioned on DATA_DRAW, unlike the exposure gates' caveat which is empty under 'planned'), containing the measured 8/8 figure and the phase-count table. This does not change the gate's fired/not-fired arithmetic (that would require measuring after the draw, contradicting the docstring's 'computed BEFORE A SINGLE STEP RUNS'); it makes the prediction's known bias direction and magnitude legible on the gate itself rather than left for a reader to rediscover.

fixed.title: draw_stream mints its per-epoch RNG stream with an unconditional again=True, disarming the duplicate-stream collision guard
fixed.what_changed: Dropped the unconditional `again=True` from the `_rng.rng_for(f"data.stream.e{epoch}", seed, again=True)` call. Nothing legitimately re-mints 'data.stream.e<n>' in one process today (the resample=False cache-hit path returns before this line for epoch>0, and each epoch has a distinct name), so the flag existed only to silence the guard against a genuine caller bug.
fixed.proof: Ran draw_stream(dat, areas, plan, epoch=0, seed=0) twice in one process with no reset_issued() between calls. BEFORE (again=True unconditional): the second call succeeded silently and st_a.bytes == st_b.bytes was True -- two 'independent' epoch-0 draws silently replayed one sequence. AFTER (again=True dropped): the second call raised spine.rng.RngError("stream 'data.stream.e0' was already issued for seed 0 ..."), restoring the guard. Also verified the resample=False cached-epoch path is unaffected: it returns before ever reaching the rng_for call, so dropping again=True changes nothing about epoch>0 replays.

fixed.title: On the REAL path a zero-size held-out block is recorded with the reason "source=synthetic holds nothing out", and nothing refuses the configuration that produced it.
fixed.what_changed: The `else` branch (n_hold == 0) used to hard-code why='source=synthetic holds nothing out' regardless of dat.source. Added a guard: on the real path, a 0-byte computed holdout now raises CorpusError naming DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC, DATA_VAL_CAP, the body length and the resulting 0, instead of silently falling through with the false synthetic-only reason string. The `else` branch is now reachable only when dat.source really is 'synthetic' (n_hold is forced to 0 there unconditionally a few lines up), so the existing reason string is correct on every path that still reaches it.

fixed.title: `seam_at` is recorded as the block offset unconditionally, so a block at offset 0 or at the tail reports a manufactured seam that does not exist -- the unreachable state the contract requires it to say.
fixed.what_changed: seam_at now reads `start if (0 < start and start + n_hold < len(blob)) else None`, with a `why` key explaining which edge (leading or tail) the block landed on when it is None -- instead of unconditionally recording `start` (a position) even when the removed block was a prefix or a suffix and manufactured no interior seam at all.
fixed.proof: Monkeypatched spine.rng.Rng.randint to always return the low bound (forcing start=0), ran open_areas at DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC=0.3 -- BEFORE: rng_holdout['eng']['seam_at'] read 0 (a position) on a block with no interior seam. AFTER: seam_at reads None with why='block landed at the body's own leading edge (offset 0): no text precedes it, so removing it manufactures no discontinuity'. An ordinary (interior) block on the same corpus still gets a numeric seam_at (verified separately, e.g. offset 1330940 on the unpatched run).

fixed.title: data.holdout_overlap is never computed, so the one instrument declared for near-duplicate contamination between the held-out block and the training body produces no number at all.
fixed.what_changed: Added `_holdout_overlap(holdout_bytes, body_bytes, n=50)`: builds a hash set of the body's 50-byte n-gram windows and reports the fraction of the holdout's own 50-byte windows that also occur in that set (None if the holdout is shorter than one window -- an unreachable reading, not a 0.0). Wired into open_areas as `rng_holdout[label]['overlap']` for every area with a nonzero holdout, closing the previously entirely-uncomputed data.holdout_overlap reading.
fixed.proof: grep -n holdout_overlap src/data/api.py BEFORE matched only the docstring's own declaration -- no field anywhere carried a value. AFTER: ran open_areas at DATA_SOURCE=real DATA_AREAS=eng,py and read rng_holdout[label]['overlap'] for both areas: eng -> 0.00082, py -> 0.01006 (both floats in [0,1], computed from a real 50-byte-window set-membership check against each area's own body). Timed the n-gram set build on a 2,000,000-byte body (the shipped DATA_CORPUS_CAP): ~0.85s, stated in the function's own docstring as the cost this pays.

fixed.title: the resample=False replay cache is keyed by id(areas), an address CPython reuses, so the stated per-Areas isolation does not hold and every Stream is retained forever
fixed.what_changed: _REPLAY's values are now `(weakref.ref(areas, evict_callback), Stream)` pairs instead of a bare Stream, still keyed by id(areas) (Areas itself is unhashable -- it has dict fields -- so it cannot be a WeakKeyDictionary key directly). The read path checks `ref() is areas` before trusting a hit, closing the id-reuse collision; the weakref's callback pops its own id() entry the moment that Areas is actually collected, closing the unbounded-retention half of the finding (every resample=False Stream used to live for the rest of the process).
fixed.proof: Built an Areas/Plan/Stream at DATA_RESAMPLE=0, captured id(areas), deleted the objects and ran gc.collect(). BEFORE (plain dict keyed by id(areas), no eviction): the entry would remain in _REPLAY forever and a later object landing on the freed id would silently receive the stale cached Stream (reproduced separately: a small repro that frees and reallocates small objects reused an id within single-digit allocations). AFTER: `old_id in data_api._REPLAY` was True right after the draw and False after gc.collect() -- the weakref callback evicted the entry the moment the Areas was actually collected, and the read path additionally checks `ref() is areas` before trusting any hit, so a same-id-different-object collision can no longer return someone else's bytes even in the window before the callback runs.

not_fixed.title: open_areas and draw_stream produce none of the counters and gates their DID IT FIRE blocks declare, so DATA's armed-but-0 and unreachable states are indistinguishable everywhere
not_fixed.detail: The declared DID IT FIRE surface is large (open_areas: data.area_open, data.area_nested, data.area_path_refused, data.area_label_collision, data.corpus_cap_trip, data.holdout_block, data.holdout_seam, data.holdout_overlap, data.val_cap_trip, data.area_refused; draw_stream: data.stream_draw, data.segment, data.contig_wrap, data.resample, data.phase_entered) and a faithful implementation needs a `counters`/`gates` field on BOTH Areas and Stream, populated correctly at every declared decision point. I made real, verified progress adjacent to this (Stream.draws for the stream's own draw count, Plan.counters for data_plan's three declared readings, and rng_holdout now carrying seam_at/overlap/why per area, which already answers data.holdout_block/data.holdout_seam/data.holdout_overlap without a new top-level field), but did not implement the comprehensive Areas.counters/Stream.counters surface this finding asks for. Two of the declared items also have genuinely ambiguous semantics I did not want to guess at under time pressure: data.resample and data.stream_draw appear to need a cross-call accumulator (similar to areas.cursors) rather than anything one draw_stream call can report alone, since a single call cannot see how many OTHER epochs in the same run redrew vs replayed. Given the size of the rest of the work list, I judged completing the remaining well-scoped items correctly was a better use of the remaining budget than a partial, semantically-uncertain counters implementation across two record types.
